_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::particle_pd#7, which execution FALSIFIED. The entry said INITRADIUS must equal dx/2 or mass and volume come out wrong. On upstream particle_sph_2d_pdbody_gravity.4C.yaml a tenfold INITRADIUS on BOTH materials leaves all ten result tests passing with abs(diff) exactly 0.00000000000000000e+00 and the bond count unchanged at 1512: the run is bit-identical, so INITRADIUS is inert for PD. 4C also never prints a total system mass at startup, so the quoted Signal cannot be read anywhere. What does carry the mass is INITIALPARTICLESPACING in PARTICLE DYNAMIC/SPH (mass = INITDENSITY * spacing^KERNEL_SPACE_DIM); doubling it breaks eight of the ten tests, which is the third arm. PD bond forces use PERIDYNAMIC_GRID_SPACING and the horizon, and PD contact gaps are measured against PERIDYNAMIC_GRID_SPACING rather than radii. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: Number of initialized peridynamic bonds on this proc: 1512

_mutation.note: remove the discriminating control: make the spacing arm identical to the baseline. Nothing then distinguishes the inert parameter from the live one, BIGSPACING_FAILURES becomes 0 and the verdict flips to yes — the fixture must go red.

invert the claim the other way: give the radius arm a spacing change instead, so what is being varied is no longer INITRADIUS. BIGRADIUS then stops being bit-identical and the exact-match count collapses — the fixture must go red.
